added.question: Does each motor shunt sit in the ESC pack's positive lead (high side) or in its return (low side)? Answer for the onboard path and for the external path. On the high side the sense leads sit at up to 67.2 V to ground; on the low side they sit within the shunt drop of ground.
added.why: IOBoard.md:469 states it as not known and names R8. It sets the common-mode voltage at the INA238's IN+ and IN− (−0.3 to 85 V, SLYS025B section 5.3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina238.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z). It also decides whether the external sense leads carry pack voltage onto the IO board's connector, which sets the voltage rating and protection of the sense input. A low-side shunt puts its drop, 15 mV at 150 A on 100 µΩ, between the ESC's return and the star ground (IOBoard.md:547).
added.for_quantity: Shunt position in the ESC pack path

added.question: When a test runs through the external path, where does that path's INA238 take the pack voltage for its VBUS input? The options are a separate voltage-sense lead from the pack, the external shunt's pack-side sense lead, or no connection, with no voltage reading on the external path.
added.why: IOBoard.md:470 states it as not known and names R8. The two paths replace each other, and only the sense leads reach the board (IOBoard.md:403-406). The page measures voltage at the pack (docs/Screens.md:131-132), and the BENCH voltage and power registers depend on it (link_pages.h:230-232). The answer decides whether the external input carries a lead at up to 67.2 V (F15). The INA238's VBUS input takes 0 to 85 V at 0.8 to 1.2 MΩ (SLYS025B 5.5, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z).

added.question: What is the highest voltage, in V, the external sense input must withstand without damage, between its two sense leads and from either lead to the board's ground? The fault cases include a sense lead on the wrong terminal, a lead off, and the load side shorted to ground.
added.why: The INA238 is rated at ±40 V between IN+ and IN− and at −0.3 to 85 V on either input (SLYS025B section 5.1, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z). Its section 7.1.4 names a short on the load side of the shunt as a case that puts the full supply voltage across the shunt. The pack reaches 67.2 V (F15), above the ±40 V limit, and the operator cables the external path for each test (IOBoard.md:405-406). Without a figure, the input in front of the fixed INA238 cannot be qualified. It may need series resistance and clamps.
added.for_quantity: External sense input fault withstand voltage

added.question: Must a port current monitor channel read current that flows back into the servo rail, from a back-driven or braking servo? If so, down to how many A in that direction? Or is a range from 0 A to the positive full scale enough?
added.why: IOBoard.md:477 states that whether a negative current is measured is not stated. The held ACS70331EESATR-2P5U3 reads 0 to 2.5 A only (ACS70331-DS Rev. 9 selection guide, https://www.allegromicro.com/-/media/files/datasheets/acs70331-datasheet.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:37:10Z). The INA3221 reads −163.84 to 163.8 mV (SBOS576C 6.5, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:35:13Z). A unidirectional replacement passes or fails on the answer.
